$comment: Per-million-token prices in USD. EVERY dollar figure contextbill reports derives from
this file, so it is versioned, dated, and cited in the report footer.
Source: Anthropic's published pricing page, read on the date in `dated` below:
https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing
These are Claude API / Microsoft Foundry / Claude Platform on AWS rates. Amazon
Bedrock and Google Vertex AI are partner-operated and priced separately -- contextbill
does not model them.
Figures here are what usage WOULD cost metered at these rates. Most Claude Code usage
is on a subscription, which bills a flat fee, so a contextbill total values the usage
rather than restating an invoice. Every surface says so.
If you are reading a report and the numbers look wrong, check `dated` below first.
A test fails once this table is more than 60 days old.
Cache writes are billed as a multiple of the model's base input rate.
5-minute TTL writes at 1.25x; 1-hour TTL writes at 2x.
TRANSCRIPTS DO NOT RECORD WHICH TTL WAS USED. `cache_creation_input_tokens` is a
single number with no TTL field, so contextbill cannot infer it and does not guess.
Default is the 5-minute rate, which is the conservative choice: if your client
actually used 1-hour caching, the reported cost is an UNDERSTATEMENT, never an
overstatement. Override with --cache-ttl=1h. The report always names which was used.

$comment-retired-models: The table below also prices retired models, because old transcripts still mention
them. Without an entry they land in unpricedModels and drop out of the total, which
understates any corpus with history. Keys are post-normalizeModelId: the dated suffix
is stripped before lookup, so `claude-opus-4-1-20250805` resolves to `claude-opus-4-1`.
This note sits outside `models` deliberately -- a `$comment` key inside that map would
be indistinguishable from a model to anything that iterates it.

claude-opus-5.note: Fast mode (usage.speed === 'fast') bills at the premium rate.

claude-opus-4-8.note: Fast mode (usage.speed === 'fast') bills at the premium rate.

claude-sonnet-5.note: $2/$10 launched as introductory pricing through 2026-08-31. The scheduled increase to $3/$15 was cancelled and $2/$10 is now the standard price.
